Posterior Mean of the Per-Period Event Probability Given History (Time-Invariant Covariates)

Source: R/G2G_static_posterior_functions.R
G2G_static_posterior_p.Rd

Updates the population distribution of the baseline rate using the number of periods a subject has survived, and returns the subject's posterior mean per-period event probability, which includes the effect of the subject's own (constant) covariate values.

Usage

G2G_static_posterior_p(solution, X_vect, hist)

Arguments

solution

A fitted model of class "G2Gcov" returned by G2G_static_MLE. Its par holds r, alpha and the coefficients on the original covariate scale (alpha already absorbs the centering used in fitting), so X_vect needs no centering or scaling.

X_vect

Covariate values for one subject. Only one set of values is accepted per call; to get curves for several subjects or covariate profiles, call the function once per profile (for example in a loop or with sapply). Either a one-row data frame containing the original covariate variables (factors and dummy variables are coded as in the fit, using the stored terms and factor levels; a missing value is an error), or plain numbers: one value per model coefficient, as a numeric vector or one-row matrix named like the coefficients (any order) or unnamed in the same order as the coefficients. If the model has a single covariate coefficient, a single number. Anything else (more than one row, or the wrong number of values) is an error.

hist

Number of periods the subject has survived without an event, a whole number >= 0. hist = 0 returns the prior mean.

Value

A single number: the posterior mean of the subject's per-period event probability given survival through hist periods.

Details

With time-invariant covariates the subject's covariate effect is the constant \(c = \exp(x'\beta)\). Surviving hist periods gives \(C(\mathrm{hist}) = \mathrm{hist} \cdot c\) and the posterior \(\lambda \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(r, \alpha + \mathrm{hist} \cdot c)\). The subject's per-period event probability is \(p = 1 - e^{-\lambda c}\), and its posterior mean is $$1 - \left(\frac{\alpha + \mathrm{hist}\, c} {\alpha + (\mathrm{hist} + 1)\, c}\right)^r.$$ This is also the probability that the subject has the event in the next period given survival through hist periods, that is, 1 minus the first step of G2G_static_cond_survival with future = 1. For a subject whose covariates are all zero (\(c = 1\)) it is the baseline probability \(p_0\).

See also

G2G_static_cond_survival, G2G_varying_posterior_p0 for the baseline probability with time-varying covariates.

Examples

# \donttest{
  if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
    library(survival)
    fit <- G2G_static_MLE(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno, data = veteran)
    # A 60-year-old with Karnofsky score 70 who has survived 30 days
    G2G_static_posterior_p(fit, data.frame(age = 60, karno = 70), hist = 30)
  }
#> [1] 0.006837165
# }
